prerequisites: Basic knowledge in programming, as taught in the basic module Object-Oriented Programming, is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to design algorithms and data structures.
Students are able to assess and estimate effort.
Students are able to apply abstraction techniques.
Students have knowledge in the analysis, design, and realization of software.
Students can follow scientific working methods (recognizing, formulating, solving problems, training abstraction skills).
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of algorithms and data structures: Design principles, Complexity, Asymptotic analysis
Elementary data structures: Lists, Stacks, Queues, Sets, Trees, Maps, Strings, Graphs
Elementary algorithms: Searching, Sorting, Inserting, Deleting, Transformations and Traversals
Implementation variants: Balanced trees, Hashsets, Huffman Codes
Polymorphic (generic) data structures: Containers and Iterators
Advanced programming techniques, e.g.: Thread programming, Design Patterns

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solution for at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution of at least two of the exercise assignments. Grading is done on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Computer Science program.
